author: Four Peaks Observatory
about: Corrections to names and surface brightness that OpenNGC v20260501 gets wrong, applied on top of the bundled extract. `name` replaces the object's name (the old one stays as an alias unless dropped); `dropNames` removes names and aliases; `surfaceBrightness` replaces the surface brightness. Each entry says why. See docs/reference/planner-catalog.md.

entries.name: IC 434
entries.reason: OpenNGC names IC 434 the Flame Nebula. IC 434 is the emission strip behind the Horsehead (its own OpenNGC note says so); the Flame Nebula is NGC 2024.

entries.name: Flame Nebula
entries.reason: NGC 2024 is the Flame Nebula; OpenNGC leaves it unnamed (see IC 434).

OpenNGC gives the Sculptor Dwarf Spheroidal a surface brightness of 19.51, brighter than any real galaxy in the file and about 4 magnitudes off (a dwarf spheroidal's mean V-band surface brightness is about 23.5; McConnachie 2012, Astronomical Journal 144, 4, Table 4). Uncorrected it scores the top brightness mark and reaches tonight's top 20. The magnitude and size in the file were not changed.
